dossier.public_summary: The dip matches the star's own 4-day spot rotation period and its depth changes from sector to sector and even transit to transit, including negative depths, while the star shows a strong brightness swing at this period. This pattern is expected from rotating starspots, not a planet transit, even though the centroid is on the target itself.

reasons.why: Phase curve as large as the transit itself (ratio ~0.95) with chi2 1729 indicates stellar variability close to the orbital period, not a planet transit.
Period matches the star's spot rotation period (0.9946x) with huge modulation amplitudes, so dip is at a rotational multiple consistent with spots, not an independent orbit.

Depth varies enormously between sectors and within the same SPOC 2-min source (from ~-62 to 1399 ppm), incompatible with a constant-depth planet; single-sector depths would correspond to different stellar densities.
